newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was rather uneven throughout the week as early trading was weak on most cuts, but did improve late in the trading week on light to moderate demand, USDA said.

Retail interest was rather slow for immediate needs but did improve somewhat as the week progressed. Chuck and round cuts struggled early to find a level, but traded at higher price levels at the end of the week on continued light demand.
Rib and loin cuts, especially the heavier cuts were under pressure throughout the week, with a few premiuns paid on the lighter middle meat cuts.

Closely trimmed items follow somewhat the same pattern generally weak on light demand. Beef trimmings traded lower early in the week, demand was rather slow early. Improved demand was noted as the week progressed, trading began active at the lower price levels. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady most of the week with fairly good demand on the fed cattle grinds.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 1.00 to 4.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal 1.00 to 4.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal generally steady; Select and Choice loin primal .50 to 1.50 higher; Closely trimmed items generally steady; Beef trimmings 1.00 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.
The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up .24 at 103.69; 700/850 Up .04 at 103.30; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.52 at 97.68; 700/850 Up .03 at 95.45.

COW and BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT Slaughter cow numbers increased this week especially in the south and southeastern regions. This, coupled with light demand for boneless processing beef, caused supplies to build up. As a result of heavy supplies and light demand, boneless beef continued to be under pressure and traded lower.

Despite moderate to heavy supplies of cow carcasses, prices were steady on moderate demand. On the other hand, cow cuts continue to be under pressure as demand was light on moderate to heavy supplies.

Utility generally steady; Cutter carcasses not established; 90% boneless beef 4.00-5.00 lower in the Midwest, Texas 3.00-4.00 lower; 85% 3.00-4.00 lower; 75% weak; 65% 4.00-5.00 lower. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, August 14, 1997 was estimated at 75.56 per cwt., down 3.19 from a week ago Friday.
